input.prompt: Repaint the reference as a REAL vintage ceramic DIP EPROM, keeping exactly the same layout, sizes and positions: the body is a real two-part ceramic CERDIP package: a pale grey-white matte ceramic lid with fine speckled sintered texture, a slightly chamfered edge, a thin dark glass-frit seal seam visible all along the bottom and side edges between the lid and the base ceramic, a small semicircular pin-1 notch cut into the middle of the LEFT end of the body, and a tiny round pin-1 dimple near the top left corner; real gold-plated DIP pins along the top and bottom edges, each pin with its narrow shoulder where it leaves the seal, evenly spaced, identical. LEFT: the same flat empty square gold plate in the upper left; below it a bare blank stretch of ceramic. MIDDLE: the same flat empty black epoxy label panel with its thin gold border. RIGHT END: a shallow gold-plated square cavity, and in it a large square SILICON DIE that fills the cavity almost completely: the die is a real chip die shot like a microscope photograph of a real EPROM or microcontroller die: a ring of square aluminium bond pads all around its edge, a thin seal ring at its border, input/output cells behind the pads, and inside them dense real circuitry: rectangular SRAM and EPROM memory arrays as fine regular grids, rows of standard cells, metal routing buses running between the blocks, in the iridescent violet, green, gold and grey thin-film colours of real silicon. Short fine gold bond wires arc from the die's pads to the bonding fingers of the cavity. Painted comic book illustration with crisp ink outlines and fine grain, the same style, light and colours as the reference; one warm golden key light from the top left; the chip alone on a pure black void, a thin green rim light on the left edge and a thin red rim light on the right edge. Seen perfectly straight on from above, horizontal, symmetric, every edge straight. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no symbols, no flags, no printed markings anywhere.
